title: Quentin and the Autopsy
premise: Quentin Nakamura, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, discovers that the diary of missing parishioner Marisol Vega continues in a different hand after her disappearance — someone is writing her life for her, and the final entry predicts Quentin's own death. Following the diary's coded references, Quentin uncovers a ledger of the cathedral's founding families hidden in the crypt's memorial brasses, revealing that Marisol discovered she was the illegitimate heir to the Vane fortune and that the current trustees have been laundering its income through the parish for decades. As the trustees close in, Quentin finds Marisol alive, hiding in the crypt with proof, and together they expose the conspiracy at the cathedral's anniversary service. The law arrives too late to be the hero; justice comes from witnesses who refuse to stay silent, and the found family of misfit parish staff becomes Marisol's true inheritance.
about_author: Hazel Nystrom is the pen name of a former parish administrator who spent eleven years cataloguing church records in northern England before turning to crime fiction. They write mysteries about quiet institutions hiding loud secrets, and about the strangers who become family in the pews.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes daily life among the cathedral archives: dust, ledgers, the crypt sealed since 1974, and the small found family of verger, organist, and candle-wax volunteer. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness, ending when police arrive asking about Marisol Vega, a parishioner Quentin knew only by her borrowing habits.

chapters.title: Borrowed Hours
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Flashback woven through present: Marisol's weekly visits, her questions about the founding families, the afternoon she stopped coming. Police find nothing; the case stalls. Emotional beat: guilt — Quentin realizes they answered her questions without wondering why she asked.

chapters.title: A Diary That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sorting Marisol's donated effects, Quentin finds her diary — and entries dated weeks after her disappearance, describing Quentin by name. The handwriting is subtly wrong. Emotional beat: cold dread; the archive that was sanctuary becomes a trap.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Quentin and an anonymous diarist. The diarist's entries reveal intimate knowledge of the cathedral's routines. Quentin compares scripts against old parish registers and confirms forgery. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve — someone wants to be caught, or wants Quentin blamed.

chapters.title: The Verger Knows Something
chapters.summary: Verger Tom Okafor's POV. Tom saw a trustee, Edmund Vane-Harcourt, in the crypt corridor the night Marisol vanished but told no one, ashamed of his own reason for being there. Emotional beat: complicity; his silence has been a stone he carries.

chapters.title: Brass and Memory
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Studying memorial brasses against the diary's odd marginal numbers, Quentin recognizes a cipher keyed to birth-and-death dates. The first decoded line names a trust. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill curdling as the pattern implies the ledger was meant to be found by whoever inherited it.

chapters.title: The Vane Fortune
chapters.summary: Organist Priya Raman's POV. Priya researches the trust online and finds decades of quiet payments routed through the parish accounts — money that kept the cathedral's roof on. Emotional beat: dread of what exposure would cost the community she loves.

chapters.title: Entry Forty-One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A new diary entry appears inside the locked archive room itself, predicting Quentin will 'go down to the crypt on Friday.' Someone has keys. Emotional beat: violation and paranoia; every colleague becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, tense and compressed. Quentin defies the entry, descends deliberately, and finds fresh air moving where no vent should be — a second entrance behind the founder's tomb. Emotional beat: courage as choice; the trap becomes a door.

chapters.title: What Marisol Found
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, first appearance. Interleaved with her disappearance: how she learned the trustees were her father's family, how she copied the ledger, how she realized they'd kill to keep it buried. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Second Entrance
chapters.summary: Tom's POV. Tom confesses his secret to Quentin: he'd been meeting Marisol there; she asked him to keep the passage quiet while she gathered proof. He believed she'd left town. Emotional beat: grief and relief braided together — she may be alive.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Full decryption of the brass-ledger: the trustees have skimmed the Vane inheritance for three generations, and Marisol is the lawful heir. Emotional beat: righteous anger at theft dressed as tradition.

chapters.title: Edmund Calls
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Vane-Harcourt visits the archive, courteous and chilling, offering Quentin a funded fellowship abroad — the same offer, Quentin realizes, made implicitly to Marisol. Emotional beat: the velvet menace of institutional power.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She discovers the trustees plan to declare the cathedral financially insolvent and sell the crypt land once Marisol is declared dead. She must choose between warning Quentin and protecting her job. Emotional beat: loyalty outweighing self-preservation.

chapters.title: Signal in the Candle Smoke
chapters.summary: Candle-volunteer Wren's POV. Wren notices votive candles lit in an impossible pattern — Marisol's old signal from their volunteering days. She's alive, and asking for paper and ink. Emotional beat: hope arriving sideways, through small domestic details.

chapters.title: Down
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Through the second entrance, Quentin finds Marisol living in the crypt's ossuary annex, ill and unyielding, guarded by the diary she kept writing to lure the trustees into overconfidence. Emotional beat: reunion without romance — two stubborn people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Plan
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts across the found family. They cannot trust police (one trustee's brother is a magistrate), so they plan to read the ledger aloud at the 400th-anniversary service, before the whole congregation and press. Emotional beat: frightened people choosing each other.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The trustees move first: the crypt is sealed again, and an 'anonymous tip' accuses Quentin of falsifying records. Quentin is suspended from the archive. Emotional beat: despair's narrow ledge — everything hinges on one service.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The service begins; Edmund watches the doors. Priya alters the music cues, Tom unlocks the crypt route, Wren seats journalists where they'll hear everything. Emotional beat: held breath; ordinary competence as resistance.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Rising from the crypt during the sermon, gaunt and unmistakable, Marisol reads the ledger's names and sums aloud as Quentin distributes photocopied pages down the pews. Edmund lunges; Tom bars the way. Emotional beat: catharsis — silence breaking like glass.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Arrests, audits, a magistrate recused. The diary's final entry, in Marisol's own hand at last, closes the false narrative. Emotional beat: exhaustion and tenderness; justice arrived late and imperfect, but arrived.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue tone. Marisol, heir now, endows the archive and asks Quentin to keep it — not as a vault but open to the parish. The crypt door stays unlocked. Emotional beat: belonging; the found family becomes the estate, and the story ends on light through the brass.
